messages:
Sam L: good morning — quick sunrise watch handoff. ran through the overnight pages, leaving a couple follow-ups. TL;DR: KV cache eviction noise in eu-west, transient increased 503s for a small set of customers, autoscaler oscillation briefly in embeddings. primary = Sam L, secondary = Nora Chen. coverage until 1500 UTC.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] 03:12 UTC - 503 spike (route: /v1/generate) — paging team. link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-042

Sam L: timeline summary: 03:12 alert, 03:18 initial mitigations (greened a canary route), 03:27 found KV eviction pressure on eu-west leader -> fallback to read-replica. by 04:00 503 rate down to baseline.

Nora Chen: note — the eviction was tied to a background shard rebalance that coincided with a heavy prefix load from a customer-run job. I left a note on the customer's tenant, asking them to spread the load.

Leo Park: actions we took:
- bumped eviction threshold on the affected leader (temporary)
- enabled prefix-KV caching on route for 2h (to reduce load)
- disabled autoscaler cooldown override (it was set to 30s, we reverted to 5m)

Maya R: metrics snapshot attached in the thread (see grafana links):
- 503 p95 peaked at 1.8% of requests during the spike
- kv_eviction_rate on leader node spiked to 120 evictions/min
- embedding-autoscaler triggered 3 up/down cycles within 10m

Sam L: current status:
- Customer-facing impact: limited; a few tenants saw degraded responses for ~15-40 minutes, support already notified.
- System health: degraded->recovering. No nodes offline.
- Autoscaler: stable after cooldown revert.

Alex V: open items for today:
1) runbook follow-up: update runbook `cache-eviction` with the eu-west leader rebalance notes (I filed a PR). link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction
2) add a canary for heavy-prefix jobs to avoid simultaneous rebalance + job spikes
3) investigate tenant job scheduling at infra level (contact SEs)

Sam L: immediate next steps for incoming shift (Nora primary):
- Nora, keep the temporary eviction threshold until 09:30 UTC unless we see new evictions.
- Check `kv_leader_rebalance` alerts and annotate any correlation with TENANT_A heavy job (ticket #TKT-558).
- If 503 rate rises above 1% sustained for 5m, escalate to oncall-sre and engage platform patch rollback.

Nora Chen: ack — I'll watch the alert rule and will coordinate with Maya if metrics trend upward. tagging @Maya R for visibility. :eyes:

Maya R: I'll run a quick sweep of autoscaler logs and post the clipped logs if I find repeated cooldown flaps.

Sam L: runbook snippets (copied for quick use):
```
# quick mitigation steps - cache eviction
1) identify leader node: `kubectl get pods -l role=kv-leader -o wide`
2) enable temp eviction-tolerance: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/tune -d '{"eviction_threshold":0.85}'`
3) enable prefix caching on route: `rb config route-ttl --route /v1/generate --ttl 120`
4) revert after 2h or once eviction_rate < 5/min
```

Leo Park: customers & comms: support emailed impacted tenants at 04:20 UTC. No escalations to legal/compliance required. CX flagged one high-value tenant; I've assigned a follow-up to account-eng (#AE-772).

Sam L: risks: if we keep high eviction tolerance too long we could increase memory pressure elsewhere. so plan is a 2-hour window + post-mortem.

Nora Chen: notes for handoff checklist:
- primary/secondary: Nora (primary), Sam (secondary fallback)
- pager policy: escalate at sustained 1% 503 for 5m or eviction_rate > 50/min for 3m
- runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction , https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-thrash
- customer tickets: TKT-558, AE-772

Sam L: post-mortem plan: I started an outline, will drop in #postmortems and invite the infra crew. target for draft by EOD.

Maya R: quick log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[03:22:11] kv-leader-7: eviction=138/min mem=72%
[03:23:02] autoscaler: scale_up -> scale_down -> scale_up (within 180s)
[03:24:45] route:/v1/generate 503 spike -> 1.8%
```

Sam L: anything else before I hand back?

Alex V: small ask — add a short note in the console alert message so oncall can see tenant id in the alert title (helps faster comms). Filed INF-321.

Nora Chen: thanks Sam, taking over now. I'll post updates here if anything changes. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: note: outgoing handoff recorded by oncall-bot at 05:10 UTC.

Sam L: thanks all — leaving monitoring and the runbook links in pinned items.
